HDF5 datasets are extremely slow at reading data by arbitrary lists of indices because each index requires a separate disk I/O operation.

The `HDF5Matrix.__getitem__` method in `keras/utils/io_utils.py` needs to be improved to handle list/ndarray-based indexing more efficiently. Instead of directly passing the list of indices to `self.data[idx]` (which does O(n) individual HDF5 reads), it should:
1. Sort the unique indices
2. Group consecutive indices into contiguous ranges (slices)
3. Read each contiguous slice at once (which is very fast - O(1) per slice)
4. Re-order the results to match the original index order

This optimization would reduce the number of HDF5 read operations from O(n) (one per sample) to O(k) where k is the number of contiguous chunks (much smaller than n).

Also, the fix could improve the training loop's shuffle behavior for HDF5 data, but the main fix is in `HDF5Matrix.__getitem__`.
